findings.source_passage: Her face was sad and lovely with bright things in it, bright eyes and a bright passionate mouth, but there was an excitement in her voice
findings.source_locator: paragraph describing Daisy's voice, after Baker introduction
findings.why_it_matters: The draft drops 'bright eyes and a bright passionate mouth' from the description, reducing a carefully constructed anaphoric image ('bright things in it, bright eyes and a bright passionate mouth') to a bare clause. The triple 'bright' repetition is a minor but characteristic stylistic signature.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full phrase: 'Her face was sad and lovely with bright things in it, bright eyes and a bright passionate mouth.'

findings.source_passage: I must have stood for a few moments listening to the whip and snap of the curtains and the groan of a picture on the wall.
findings.source_locator: interior scene, after the two women are described on the couch
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence—with its sensory precision and Nick's dreamlike passivity—is a characteristic voice moment establishing the enchanted strangeness of the Buchanan house. Its omission flattens the hallucinatory quality of the scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence between the description of the two women and Tom shutting the windows.

findings.source_passage: To a certain temperament the situation might have seemed intriguing—my own instinct was to telephone immediately for the police.
findings.source_locator: after 'this fifth guest's shrill metallic urgency out of mind'
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of Nick's sharpest ironic asides and a voice-defining moment of sardonic understatement; its loss erases a signature register marker and diminishes Nick's characterization as an ironic observer.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence as Nick's ironic reaction to the telephone situation.

findings.source_passage: I never saw this great-uncle, but I'm supposed to look like him—with special reference to the rather hard-boiled painting that hangs in father's office.
findings.source_locator: family background paragraph, before Yale graduation
findings.why_it_matters: The detail of the 'hard-boiled painting' is a small but characteristic self-deprecating Fitzgerald touch; its omission is minor but the draft loses a moment of dry humor from Nick's self-presentation.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the sentence about the great-uncle and the hard-boiled painting when compressing the family background.

findings.source_passage: The lamplight, bright on his boots and dull on the autumn-leaf yellow of her hair, glinted along the paper as she turned a page with a flutter of slender muscles in her arms.
findings.source_locator: interior scene, Tom and Jordan with the Saturday Evening Post
findings.why_it_matters: The draft reduces the Post-reading scene to a bare summary, losing a signature prose-visual image of Jordan Baker that the critical tradition has noted as characteristic of Fitzgerald's painterly style.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the lamplight sentence describing Jordan turning the page.

summary: The draft is largely faithful, preserving all major signatures verbatim (opening lines, Gatsby introduction, 'beautiful little fool,' green light closing), but suffers three medium-severity voice/register losses in the Buchanan interior that flatten Nick's ironic narrator consciousness without triggering regeneration.
